messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwise.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: FinWise | Post-call: performance SLOs & next steps (load test coordination)

Hi Alex/Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment before the customer-led load test: 

Summary of what we heard from FinWise:
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end < 300ms for non-streaming completion requests; for streaming token-by-token delivery you indicated p95 for token latency < 120ms (important for your live-update UI).
- Throughput & concurrency: target sustained concurrency ~200 connections, peak bursts to 400 for short windows. Estimated token throughput target ~8k tokens/sec across the test.
- Streaming: we'll need to validate both streaming and non-streaming flows.
- Success criteria: error rate < 1% and p95 <= target across the test window.

Redwood asks / proposed plan: 
1) Customer-led load test window — suggested slot: Tue Mar 24, 02:00–04:00 UTC (overnight for your users). Please confirm.
2) Test artifacts: we usually ask for your k6/Locust script (we received a draft today — thanks). Attachments: I attached our template (k6_finwise_test_script.js) and our proposed load_test_plan.pdf.
3) Test account & endpoint: we can provision a short-lived test API key and staging endpoint (rw-staging.redwood.ai) that mirrors the production config. Rishi will share the test API key and IP ranges to whitelist.
4) Ramp plan & observability: recommend 10min ramp, 30–45min steady at target concurrency, 10min cool-down. Please capture p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput, and streaming token latency. We'll ingest your k6 metrics into our dashboard for side-by-side comparison.
5) Security/compliance: you asked to limit logs and not send PII. We'll ensure request bodies are redacted and logs marked as test.

Action items: 
- Alex/Priya: confirm test window and the exact k6 script you'll run (we received a draft; please attach final).
- Rishi: provision test API key, staging endpoint, and IP allowlist.
- Marissa: coordinate availability on the 24th and run the post-test review.

Attachments: k6_finwise_test_script.js (template), finwise_slo_requirements.xlsx (your SLO doc).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FinWise | Post-call: performance SLOs & next steps (load test coordination)

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks correct. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side: 

1) SLO clarification: our product team is targeting p95 <= 300ms for non-streaming end-to-end completions. For streaming, it's a bit different — we care about token delivery latency and the UI has a budget of ~120ms p95 per token as you noted.
2) Throughput: our expected steady baseline is ~200 concurrent clients; during peak scenarios we can see short bursts up to ~400. Total tokens/sec goal for the test: ~8,000 tokens/s.
3) Test window: Tue Mar 24, 02:00–04:00 UTC works for us.
4) Test script: attaching our k6 script (k6_finwise_test_script.js) — it's the draft you referenced. We'll finalize it tonight; mostly it runs both streaming and non-streaming cases.
5) Allowlist: we need the IP ranges and test key to be shared so our infra team can finalize firewall rules and have them peer-reviewed (I'll loop SRE).
6) Logs: we appreciate the redaction note — for the test we only need agg metrics and latency traces.

CC'ing our SRE to pick up the IP allowlist step.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Integrations, FinWise
alex.johnson@finwise.com

Hi Alex — thanks, this is clear. I've provisioned the staging environment and added details below. Please circulate to your SRE for allowlist rules.

Staging endpoint & credentials:
- Endpoint: https://rw-staging.finwise.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Test API key (expires 2026-03-25): rw-test-key-FW-8342-XXXX
- Model for test: redwood-serve-rlhf-v2 (production-equivalent config for inference — we can switch to a smaller variant if you want to test quantized execution)

IP allowlist (please whitelist these ranges for the test window):
- 52.23.14.0/24
- 34.201.10.0/24
- 3.120.45.0/24
- 18.205.88.0/23

Recommended k6 run (we reviewed your draft script and attached a tuned version):
- Ramp: 10 minutes (linear) to 200 VUs
- Steady: 30 minutes at 200 VUs (simulate both streaming and non-streaming flows)
- Burst: run a 10-minute ramp to 400 VUs once during the steady window to capture tail behavior
- Cooldown: 10 minutes
- Metrics to capture: request latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput (tokens/sec), streaming token latency (we'll capture per-chunk recv times), connection open latency, and any 5xx/429 errors.

Notes / caveats:
- KV caching: if your script exercises repeated prompts we recommend enabling prefix caching on the staging key (we have it off by default) — let me know if you want caching on to simulate warm-state traffic.
- Token accounting: k6 will emit request-level times; for streaming token latency we instrument per-chunk arrival times in the script (see attached k6_finwise_test_script.js).
- Observability: we'll stream k6 metrics to the Redwood dashboard and share a read-only link during/after the test.

Attachments: updated k6_finwise_test_script.js (tuned for ramp/burst), load_test_plan.pdf (detailed steps).

If the IP ranges and test key look good, we'll finalize the allowlist and I'll ask ops to enable the staging key at 01:55 UTC on Mar 24.

Rishi
